items.prompt: In "That bag is mine," which word is a possessive pronoun?

options.why: This is a noun, the thing that is owned.
This points to the bag. It is not the owner word.
This is a verb.

hints: Which word tells you who owns the bag?
A possessive pronoun stands in for the owner and the thing.
Look for the word that could replace "my bag".
items.explanation: Mine tells us who owns the bag and stands alone, so it is a possessive pronoun.

items.prompt: Dewi and Putri painted the poster. It is ___.
hints: The pronoun comes at the end with no noun after it.
Their needs a noun after it. Which word can stand alone?
Try "It is their poster" and "It is theirs".
items.explanation: Theirs stands alone at the end of the sentence. Their must be followed by a noun, like their poster.

items.prompt: Which sentence makes clear who won?

options.text: Bayu told Leo that he had won.
options.why: He could mean Bayu or Leo.

options.text: He told him that he had won.
options.why: All three pronouns could refer to either boy.

options.text: Bayu told Leo that they had won.
options.why: They could mean both boys or other people, so it is unclear.

hints: Check each pronoun: could it mean two people?
Clear writing avoids a pronoun with two possible owners.
Use direct speech or a name instead of he.
items.explanation: Using direct speech removes the confusion: you clearly means Leo.

hints: Think about whether the word needs a noun after it.
You can say "That is ours." but not "That is our."
Say "___ book" and "The book is ___" to test.
items.explanation: Ours, yours and theirs can stand alone. Our, your and their need a noun after them.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence with one pronoun. The red umbrella belongs to Hadi, so the red umbrella is ___.
hints: One word replaces "Hadi's".
Hadi is a boy.
Which possessive pronoun means belonging to him?
items.explanation: His can stand alone and replaces Hadi's: the umbrella is his.

items.prompt: I have ___ coins than you, so I have ___ money.
hints: Coins can be counted. Money is thought of as an amount.
Use fewer for things you can count.
Use less for things you cannot count one by one.
items.explanation: Fewer goes with countable nouns such as coins. Less goes with uncountable nouns such as money.

items.prompt: Which word is an abstract noun?

options.why: You can touch a table, so it is a concrete noun.
You can see a river, so it is a concrete noun.
A teacher is a person, so it is a concrete noun.

hints: Abstract nouns name ideas or feelings.
You cannot touch or see an abstract noun.
Which word is a quality, not a thing?
items.explanation: Bravery is an idea. You cannot touch it, so it is an abstract noun.

hints: Can you touch it or see it?
Abstract nouns name ideas, feelings or qualities.
Try the word "a" before each noun and ask if you can hold it.
items.explanation: Kindness, freedom and honesty are ideas. Bicycle, mango and window are things you can touch.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses fewer or less correctly?

options.text: There were less people at the market.
options.why: People can be counted, so use fewer.
Traffic is uncountable, so use less.

options.text: We have fewer chairs than we need.
He ate fewer rice than me.
options.why: Rice is uncountable, so use less.

hints: Is the noun countable or uncountable?
Fewer goes with things you count one by one.
Think: can you say "one chair, two chairs"?
items.explanation: Chairs can be counted, so fewer is right. Traffic and rice are uncountable, so they take less.

items.prompt: Joko saw Hadi at the gate. He was holding a kite. Joko was the one holding the kite. Which one word replaces "He" so the meaning is clear?
hints: He could mean either boy.
The best fix is to use a name.
Which name holds the kite?
items.explanation: Replacing He with Joko removes the confusion, so the reader knows who held the kite.

items.prompt: Complete the table of abstract nouns.
head: Adjective
Abstract noun
hints: Each adjective turns into a noun for the quality.
Look at the ending: -ness, -ry and -dom are all noun endings.
Start with brave. Which ending does it take?
items.explanation: Brave becomes bravery, wise becomes wisdom and free becomes freedom.

items.prompt: What is unclear about this sentence? Kofi helped Leo carry the boxes, and then he went home.

options.why: Boxes is correct because more than one was carried.
Helped is right because it happened in the past.
Then is the correct word for the order of events.

hints: Which word stands in for a person?
Count the possible people the pronoun could refer to.
Check what he points back to.
items.explanation: He could mean either boy. A name such as Kofi or Leo would make it clear.

options.why: My needs a noun after it, so it is not a possessive pronoun.
Their needs a noun after it.

hints: A possessive pronoun can stand alone.
Test each one in "The book is ___."
Which words cannot end the sentence "The book is ___."?
items.explanation: Mine, hers and theirs can stand alone. My and their must come before a noun.

items.answer: The picnic basket is hers, not mine.
hints: The sentence has a comma.
Two possessive pronouns stand alone in it.
Start with The.
items.explanation: Hers and mine both stand alone and show who owns the basket.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses a possessive pronoun correctly?

options.why: Our needs a noun after it. Use ours.
Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe.

options.text: Is that bike yours or theirs?

options.why: Their needs a noun after it. Use theirs.

hints: Possessive pronouns stand alone and have no apostrophe.
Check each sentence for a noun after the pronoun.
Which options end with a correct stand-alone word?
items.explanation: Yours and theirs stand alone and have no apostrophe. The other sentences use the wrong form.
